newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria launches tax probe into clearing bank.
newsitem.headline: Austria launches tax probe into clearing bank.

text.p: Austrian tax authorities said on Tuesday they had launched an investigation into Kontrollbank, the country's only clearing bank, following allegations it had made an undeclared payment to its shareholders.

"We are examining Kontrollbank (OeKB)," Reinhard Stoeger, head of the Vienna tax office's corporate tax department, told Reuters. "It concerns a suspected secret profit transfer. We started to act immediately following reports in the media."
He said the alleged transfer was "one of several areas" investigated by the tax authorities. He declined to give any further details on which other areas were being probed.

Austrian opposition parties have alleged that the suicide of OeKB board member Gerhard Praschak last week was linked to a tax evasion scandal by the OeKB involving a secret payout of 140 million schillings ($12 million).

Documents mailed by Praschak before his death to opposition parties and the prosecutor's office contained handwritten notes in which details of the alleged payments to OeKB's shareholders -- Austrian commercial banks -- were outlined. Copies of the documents were made available to reporters.
In the notes, Praschak charged that key shareholders Bank Austria and Creditanstalt pressed for the payment to be disguised as fees on credit lines to be opened to OeKB by the banks.
Bank Austria strongly denied the accusations. The country's leading bank said that all payments to or from OeKB had been properly documented and that no secret payments were made.

Tax office spokesman Stoeger said the inquiry into the affair was unlikely to yield results soon. "The inquiry will take weeks and months. We'll see whether there is something to the allegations," he said.

The opposition Liberal Forum on Tuesday asked the government to respond to allegations that political pressure on Praschak over board changes had contributed to his suicide. The party also repeated its call on the government to relinquish its influence in the banking sector.
